title: Binomial Coefficient Modulo Small Prime
description: Given non-negative 64-bit integers `n` and `k` (`0 <= k <= n <= 10^15`) and a prime integer `p` (`2 <= p <= 10^5`), compute the binomial coefficient `C(n, k) % p`, where `C(n, k) = n! / (k! * (n - k)!)`. Because `n` can greatly exceed `p`, ordinary factorial tables up to `n` are infeasible and `n!` may be divisible by `p`.
constraints: p is guaranteed to be a prime number.
hints: By Lucas's Theorem, `C(n, k) == C(n % p, k % p) * C(n // p, k // p) (mod p)`, where `C(a, b) = 0` whenever `b > a`.
Precompute factorials `fact[0..p - 1]` and inverse factorials `invFact[0..p - 1]` modulo `p` using Fermat's Little Theorem (`fact[p - 1]^(p - 2) mod p`) via fast exponentiation.

examples.explanation: C(10, 3) = 120, which is divisible by 3, so the result is 0.
In base 2, 7 is 111 and 3 is 011; every base-2 digit satisfies k_i <= n_i, so C(7, 3) = 35 == 1 (mod 2).
